author: OpenAI GPT-6, tool-mediated source assessment
scope_note: Only the listed pages and publisher metadata were consulted. The 2013 official journal-hosted PDF and separately a third-party published-layout copy showed the same printed page anchors on pp. 222, 224, 255, 256; byte identity was not tested. The 2006 article body, 2008/2013 monograph and full 2013 article were not read. No original PDF bytes were downloaded or SHA-256 checked.

observations.locator: first printed page, header and title; footnote 1
observations.finding: tripleC 1(1), 2003, pp. 71-94; 24-page published-layout journal PDF. Footnote identifies earlier manuscript and talks; source is not a newly composed 2008 theory.

observations.locator: section on five levels, numbered list 1-5
observations.finding: The five-layer model explicitly distinguishes Firstness, causal matter, informational cybernetics, living semiosis and conscious language; machine signs are called quasi/proto-semiotic.

observations.locator: Published field and Vol. 1 No. 1 (2003) issue field
observations.finding: Issue-designated year 2003 versus journal platform online publication date 2008-06-12; neither should overwrite the other.

observations.locator: publisher-indexed title, abstract and bibliographic metadata; article body not accessed
observations.finding: Semiotica 158 (2006), pp. 255-296, different DOI and subtitle from tripleC 2003; indexed publisher abstract repeats five levels, but textual revision/duplication cannot be assessed without full text.

observations.locator: An Overview of the Flow of the Argumentation in the Article, closing lines
observations.finding: Author states article will conclude with five ontological levels; paragraph separately previews the four-armed knowledge star.

observations.locator: The Four Views of the Cybersemiotic Star and Figure 1
observations.finding: Four star arms classify types of knowing (living systems, inner experience, matter/energy, sense/meaning), not a proposed exhaustive replacement for levels of emergence.

observations.locator: The Ontological Basis of Cybersemiotics; explicitly numbered five ontological levels
observations.finding: Five levels are enumerated again in the 2013 paper: Firstness/quantum vacuum, efficient causation, protosemiotic chemical information, living signification, self-conscious language.
The 2013 figure links levels of semiosis and proto-semiosis; its caption cautions that the diagram is a simplification and not literal bodily localization.
